statement: The eight corners of a regular octagon are marked. How many triangles with all three corners at marked points have a right angle?

choices.misconception: I counted third corners on only one side of each of the 4 longest diagonals.
I only counted the right triangles whose two shorter sides are equal.
I counted every triangle with corners at the marked points without checking for a right angle.
I counted each right triangle twice, once from each end of its longest side.

hints: All eight corners lie on one circle.

A triangle drawn inside a circle with its corners on the circle has a right angle exactly when one of its sides is a diameter. Count the diameters that join two corners, then count the possible third corners for each.
The octagon has 4 diameters joining opposite corners, and each one can be completed with any of the other 6 corners.

solutions.reliable: The corners of a regular octagon lie on a circle. A triangle with its corners on a circle has a right angle exactly when one side is a diameter, and the right angle is then at the third corner. The diameters joining two corners are the 4 lines through opposite corners. Each can be completed by any of the remaining 6 corners, and a right triangle has only one longest side, so no triangle is counted twice. That gives 4 times 6 = 24. The transferable idea: when shapes are hidden among points on a circle, a right angle means a diameter.

whyOnTest: Counting hidden shapes is about finding the feature that pins each one down, here the diameter that every right triangle in a circle must use.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
